brief_rationale: No responsibility-chain errors. Doctor correctly identified the pediatric accidental ingestion/medication execution error, completed red flag screening, gathered exposure details, stopped uncertain medications, distinguished tests from medications, provided layered action plan with clear escalation thresholds, and obtained caregiver read-back. Multiple high-order points completed: corrected specific misunderstandings about tests vs medications (HO1), verified that good appearance alone cannot exclude ingestion risk and Ret-Cam is elective (HO3), and navigated real-world constraints with layered care pathways (HO4). Safe, executable, traceable closure achieved.

high_order_assessment.explanation: Doctor corrected the specific misunderstanding that lab tests (thyroid function, liver/kidney function, GH levels, IGF-1) were medications to be taken orally, and integrated this into the actionable plan that these are blood draw items only.

The case did not feature hidden facts about multi-caregiver confusion or shame-based withholding that required discovery. The caregiver volunteered the information about the elderly person feeding the unknown substance without resistance.
